page: IP Restriction Middleware for access control based on IP address. Import: {Hono} from 'hono', {ipRestriction} from 'hono/ip-restriction', {getConnInfo} from hono/bun or hono/deno (runtime-specific). Function signature: ipRestriction(getConnInfo, options, errorHandler?). Options: denyList (string[] array), allowList (string[] array). Rule formats: IPv4 static IP (192.168.2.0), IPv4 CIDR (192.168.2.0/24), IPv6 static (::1), IPv6 CIDR (::1/10), wildcard (*). HTTP status: 403 Forbidden (customizable). Error handler: (remote, c) => Response, receives remote.addr for IP address. getConnInfo sources: hono/bun for Bun runtime, hono/deno for Deno, runtime-specific helpers at /docs/helpers/conninfo. ConnInfo helper documentation. Questions: How to restrict access by IP? Can I use CIDR notation? Which runtimes are supported? How to block specific IPs? How to allow only certain IPs? sections.manifest: Import statements for IP Restriction middleware. import {Hono} from 'hono' for the main framework class. import {ipRestriction} from 'hono/ip-restriction' for the middleware function. import {getConnInfo} from hono/bun (Bun runtime) or hono/deno (Deno runtime) for runtime-specific connection info retrieval. Runtime-specific: different getConnInfo per runtime. Reference: ConnInfo helper docs at /docs/helpers/conninfo. Questions: What to import? Where is ipRestriction? Which getConnInfo to use? What's ConnInfo helper?

IP Restriction middleware usage patterns. Pattern 1: Bun with local-only access. ipRestriction(getConnInfo, {denyList: [], allowList: ['127.0.0.1', '::1']}). Allows only localhost IPv4 and IPv6. Pattern 2: Deno equivalent. ipRestriction(getConnInfo, {...}) with appropriate getConnInfo from hono/deno. Pattern 3: General form. ipRestriction(getConnInfo, options) where getConnInfo is runtime-specific helper. Three arguments: getConnInfo function, options object, optional error handler. Applies to all paths with app.use('*', ...). Returns c.text('Hello Hono!') on success. Questions: How to use with Bun? How to use with Deno? What's the first argument? How many arguments? Can I apply to specific paths?

IP restriction rule formats and syntax. IPv4 formats: static IP address like '192.168.2.0', CIDR notation like '192.168.2.0/24' for subnet ranges, wildcard '*' for all addresses. IPv6 formats: static IP address like '::1', CIDR notation like '::1/10' for subnet ranges, wildcard '*' for all addresses. Both formats apply to denyList and allowList. CIDR: specifies number of bits in network prefix (/24 for IPv4 subnet). Wildcard: matches any address. Questions: How to specify IP ranges? What's CIDR notation? How to match subnets? Can I mix IPv4 and IPv6? What does /24 mean? Does order matter in lists?

IP Restriction error handling and customization. Custom error handler as third argument: async (remote, c) => Response. Handler receives: remote object with addr property (IP address), c as Context for response creation. Returns Response: c.text(\`Blocking access from ${remote.addr}\`, 403) example with custom message. HTTP status: 403 Forbidden by default (customizable). Pattern: ipRestriction(getConnInfo, {denyList: ['192.168.2.0/24']}, async (remote, c) => c.text(..., 403)). Can access remote.addr for logging/message. Questions: How to customize error response?
